items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: Trombone player. Trombone player, I don't think. You know, I tell you about musicians now. I know gangs of musicians, but not by their name, you see

ctx.x: Sam Wooding's orchestra was there. And, um, then, uh, let me see, what other people, orchestra was there? Uh, Danny Wilson, that was Edith Wilson's husband, he had a band there. And, oh, there was two, three different bands there, you know, from a minute ago. Because, uh, Sam Wooding's and left them when they opened up the band, that Club Alabama downtown in New York, then they left the Nest to go down to the Club Alabama. That's where the Frenchman, it was a Frenchman, I think, only, he took them to Paris, he…
Did you ever know Albert Wynn? Albert Wynn?

Trombone player. Trombone player, I don't think. You know, I tell you about musicians now. I know gangs of musicians, but not by their name, you see, because it was one of those things where on the job you come in, hello, how you feeling? And that's all, you know, all I know you work where I work at, but I don't know your name, you know, see. But my piano player, usually they, I'd always, would know them, you know. Now, the reason I knew so many of Duke Ellington's boys and I never worked with them, because they…
